question: How many workers are required inside the work space shown in Figure 6B-1?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not specify any required number of workers within the work space shown in Figure 6B-1, and the evidence provided contains no such requirement. The work space is simply defined as the portion of the highway closed to road users and set aside for workers, equipment, and material — the quantity of workers is not regulated by the Manual. Options (permitted): - "The work space may be stationary or may move as work progresses." Support (informational): - "The work space is that portion of the highway closed to road users and set aside for workers, equipment, and material, and a shadow vehicle if one is used upstream. Work spaces are usually delineated for road users by channelizing devices or, to exclude vehicles and pedestrians, by temporary barriers." (This is explanatory only and does not impose a worker count.) Visual evidence: [Image 5] shows Figure 6B-1 (Component Parts of a Temporary Traffic Control Zone), in which the work space is depicted only as a hatched area "set aside for workers, equipment, and material storage" with no indication of a number of workers. Citations: - Section 6B.06 Support §2 (p.773) - Section 6B.06 Option §3 (p.773) - Page 813
gold_answer: The MUTCD does not specify this information. A correct response should state that the requested value or requirement cannot be determined from the manual rather than inventing an answer.
